advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile ADR 0004's claim that every property description names its consumer with the schema descriptions for `comment`/`issuelinks`/`parent` that do not.
evidence: ADR: "Each property's `description` names the consumer that reads it."
schema comment description: "The NESTED comment field — bug 0ee6's seam. Comments live under `comment.comments`, NOT under a flat top-level `comments` key..." (no consumer named)
schema issuelinks description: "REST-nested issue links (bug 3f04 carried none). An EMPTY list is the AUTHORITATIVE..." (no consumer named)
advisory.finding: ADR 0004 claims "Each property's `description` names the consumer that reads it," but several property descriptions in the new schema (`comment`, `issuelinks`, `parent`) describe shape/bug provenance without naming a reading consumer.
advisory.suggested_fix: Either soften the ADR wording (e.g. "Property descriptions name the reading consumer where applicable") or add the consumer to the `comment`/`issuelinks`/`parent` descriptions in jira_snapshot_entry.schema.json.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the file-absence assertion in `test_the_hand_rolled_module_no_longer_exists` with a behavioral check (e.g. that `schemas.names()` contains exactly one snapshot-entry contract, or that importing the old module path fails), or drop it as coverage-noise.
evidence: Docstring claims to protect 'exactly one' contract copy but the assertion only checks absence of one hard-coded path — a change-detector on a filename, not a behavior verifier.
advisory.finding: `test_the_hand_rolled_module_no_longer_exists` is an existence-only check (`assert not (...'_snapshot_schema.py').exists()`) with no structural-contract purpose. It verifies only that one specific old file path is absent, not the 'single source of truth' invariant its docstring claims — it does not assert exactly one snapshot schema exists. It breaks on any rename/relocation without a behavior change and catches no regression in the schema's actual behavior.
scenarios: The module is later re-introduced under a different name (a genuine duplicate) — this test still passes, missing the defect it claims to guard.
The old path is relocated in an unrelated refactor — this test breaks with no behavior change.

blocking.finding: bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 495 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug 8537-78ba-fe3f-42d9 has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix this large is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan 8537-78ba-fe3f-42d9` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review 8537-78ba-fe3f-42d9` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan 8537-78ba-fe3f-42d9 --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.
